title_english: Manuscripts of Chala Jnanoday: Sacred Buddhist Puthis of Chalapather
description: Historical Buddhist puthis and Jataka manuscripts preserved in the Chala Jnanoday Puthibharal (established in 1948 at Chalapather Shyam Gaon), documenting traditional Puthidana merit ceremonies, monastic Vinaya, and moral discourses written on Sanchipat bark.

full_translation: The historic Chala Jnanoday library was established in 1948 to safeguard ancient Tai manuscripts. Within the repository rest dozens of precious Sanchipat-bark manuscripts recording the Dhamma. The villagers perform the sacred rite of Puthidana, sponsoring the copying and public reading of manuscripts. The venerable monks recite the melodious stanzas, blessing all living beings with peace and clarity. These sacred texts instruct humanity on extinguishing sorrow and avoiding karmic misdeeds. The Three Refuges—the Buddha, the Dhamma, and the Sangha—are the supreme light of our community. Treated bark from the sacred Sanchi tree endures undiminished through centuries of humid monsoon rain. May future generations of Tai children treasure and protect these sacred manuscripts of Chalapather.
title: Manuscripts of Chala Jnanoday: Sacred Buddhist Puthis of Chalapather
